title: App-context pattern (per-record frontmatter)
description: Frontmatter of app-context/src/patterns/<slug>.md. Documents a recurring UX interaction pattern scoped to one or more Actian apps.

slug.description: Kebab-case identifier for the pattern; used as the filename (minus .md) and cross-reference target.

label.description: Human-readable display name of the UX pattern.

apps.description: App slugs where this UX pattern appears.

reference.description: What the pattern's description answers to, as the recipes' `reference` does (#716). `product`: the shipped product shows this pattern, and where the product and a design disagree the product wins; `screenshots` names where it was captured. `design`: not in the product as captured, so the description follows a design and names no screenshot.

screenshots.description: Product screenshots that show this pattern, as paths relative to app-context/src/recipes (the recipes' `derivedFrom.screenshot` convention). Only on a `product` pattern; absent where the product ships the pattern but no screenshot has captured it yet.

components.description: Registry-key slugs of the DS components this pattern composes (authored; projected to the graph as ux_pattern -> component 'uses_component' edges).

tags.description: Selection tags for this page shape. A consumer choosing a layout for a screen matches on these. Authored deliberately, because the alternative is not 'no tags': a consumer with nothing to read invents them by splitting the slug on hyphens, which joins on naming coincidence (plugin #300). Name what the shape IS and what it is FOR, not the components it happens to use; those are already in `components`. A shape that legitimately matches no archetype should stay honestly untagged rather than be given tags that force a match.

when.description: Selection guidance: when this shape applies, and which neighbouring shape to use instead when it does not. Written for whoever or whatever picks a shape. Leave it absent rather than guess: an absent `when` is a visible gap, an invented one is not. Do not restate the description here.
examples: Use when the user narrows a large collection by several independent facets at once. Do not use search-filtered-table, which is explicitly the single-search-no-facets case.
